title: OneDrive: sync up to 1 million items on macOS
summary: The rollout, eligibility, licensing context and Tier preference are supported. The control note incorrectly says the Mac deployment page does not mention Intune, although that page explicitly describes using Intune; the Intune path also stops before the preference-file configuration.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to increase Mac sync capacity from 300,000 to 1 million items per sync instance, per device.
claims.quote: We are now increasing the same item sync limit for OneDrive on macOS: from 300,000 items to 1 million items per sync instance, per device.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Non-qualifying devices retain the supported 300,000-item limit without a change in behaviour.
claims.quote: Devices that do not meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements will continue to sync at the existing supported limit of 300,000 items without disruption.

claims.claim: The Mac increase follows a Windows increase announced in MC1294528.
claims.quote: In MC1294528, we announced an increase to the item sync limit for OneDrive on Windows. We are now increasing the same item sync limit for OneDrive on macOS

claims.claim: Microsoft intends the increase to help organisations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync reliably.
claims.quote: This increase is designed to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices.

claims.claim: Public Preview precedes General Availability.
claims.quote: The capability will be available first in Public Preview for devices enrolled in the Insiders ring, and later in General Availability.

claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive macOS 1 million items preview; read the entire supplied MC1477187 and roadmap record. MC1477187 schedules Public Preview (Worldwide) only; the record gives no cloud-specific dates.

claims.quote: Ensure devices meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements (i.e., supported operating system, memory, storage, and processor).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The record and notice describe no new data source or new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: data-source and access changes in the full supplied roadmap description and MC1477187; they describe increased sync capacity for OneDrive and SharePoint libraries, with no new source or access grant.

claims.claim: The roadmap and MC1477187 describe no change to sign-in or permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: sign-in and permissions in the entire supplied roadmap description and MC1477187. Neither describes a sign-in or permission change.

claims.claim: MC1477187 states that no compliance considerations were identified.
claims.quote: No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

claims.claim: The item describes a sync-capacity change rather than an agent or new automated action.
claims.quote: OneDrive Sync supports syncing up to 1 million items on macOS devices, helping teams manage large document libraries and shared content at scale without compromising access across devices.

claims.claim: SharePoint limits recommends syncing no more than 300,000 files in one OneDrive or team site library.
claims.quote: For optimum performance, we recommend syncing no more than 300,000 files in a single OneDrive or team site library.

claims.claim: The same performance issues can occur at 300,000 items or more across all synced libraries.
claims.quote: the same performance issues can occur if you have 300,000 items or more across all libraries you're syncing, even if you aren't syncing all items in those libraries.

claims.claim: The 300,000-file soft sync limit also applies to shortcut folders.
claims.quote: The 300K file “soft” limit for OneDrive Sync also applies to shortcut folders.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The Mac App Store sync app follows a separate update process.
claims.quote: The sync app installed from the Mac App Store follows a separate update process. After we finish rolling out updates within the Production ring, we publish them to the Mac App Store, where they're immediately released to everyone.

claims.claim: Participation of the Mac App Store edition in this million-item preview is not explicitly stated.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive "macOS" "1 million" "App Store". Read Mac deployment and sync update-process pages, Office Mac App Store search excerpts, roadmap and MC1477187; no feature-specific App Store eligibility statement found.

claims.claim: Intune offers Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. Platform: Select macOS. Profile type: Select Templates > Preference file. In Configuration settings, configure your settings:
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file > Configuration settings > Property list file'. The cited Intune page places the preference-file upload there.

claims.claim: The Tier XML preference in com.microsoft.OneDriveUpdater.plist sets the Mac sync app update ring.
claims.quote:
This setting lets you specify the sync app update ring for users in your organization. ~/Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.OneDriveUpdater.plist | com.microsoft.OneDriveUpdater. <key>Tier</key>
<string>(UpdateRing)</string>

claims.claim: The Intune preference-file profile instructions require the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Intune admin center with an account that has the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.

claims.claim: The Mac page lists Insiders, Production and Enterprise, also known as Deferred.
claims.quote: first to Insiders, then to Production, and finally to Deferred. Enterprise (also known as "Deferred"): The Enterprise ring users get new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements last.

claims.claim: The Mac deployment page does not mention Intune.
claims.quote: You can use Microsoft Intune. Other common tools are Jamf Pro, Munki, and AutoPkg.
claims.fix: In controls[0].note and the rendered table note, replace 'it does not mention Intune, so confirm the profile on a test Mac' with 'its Tier section does not describe Intune deployment, so confirm the profile on a test Mac'. The Mac page does mention Intune for app deployment.

claims.claim: Devices receiving the Intune preference-file profile must be enrolled and MDM managed by Intune.
claims.quote: The device must be enrolled and MDM managed by Intune.

claims.claim: Intune does not validate property-list settings.
claims.quote: Test your changes before assigning the profile to your devices. Intune doesn't validate the settings in the property list file.

claims.claim: Users cannot change the update ring after the Tier setting is enabled and a ring selected.
claims.quote: When you enable this setting and select a ring, users aren't able to change it.
